title: Northglass Reading Room
subtitle: Fictional demo for private viewing, not a client project
summary: A fictional project used to try private viewing. It is not a real commission and it is not Allison McElroy's work.

blocks.text: This reading room is invented for the viewing page: a small library room with one glazed wall. Nothing on this page describes a real client or a built project.

sections.title: Fictional option A
sections.summary: Invented west and north walls, with the east side left open.

blocks.text:
This reading room is invented for the viewing page. Nothing here is a real client, a built room, or a measurement from a commission.

## West wall

- West wall: a 36" invented shelf over a 9'-0" bench.
- South end: a 24" fictional cabinet.

## North wall

- North wall: an 18" invented niche and a 30" fictional window, 3'-0" x 4'-0".

The east side stays open. A 5'-0" x 2'-6" invented table sits in the center. These figures exist only so the page can show labels, lists, and dimensions.

sections.title: Fictional option B
sections.summary: Invented glazed wall, roof, and window detail.

blocks.text: Another invented paragraph for the heavy demo. It talks about a glazed wall, a simple roof, and a window detail that exist only in this fixture. Use it to check that several long sections stay inside one tab and that only one tab panel is open. This is not Allison McElroy's work.

sections.title: Fictional option C
sections.summary: Invented room, mullion, and shelf for layout testing.

blocks.text: A third fictional section with enough sentences to fold. The room, the mullion, and the shelf are made up for layout testing. Opening this section should not reveal the drawings or the model file. The download and the full viewer stay on their own tab.

sections.title: Fictional option D
sections.summary: Filler about paper, ink, and spacing.

blocks.text: Fourth invented section. It is here so a phone-width page can show a short tab bar instead of a long list of links. The words are filler about paper, ink, and spacing. No address, client, or real dimension belongs in this paragraph.

sections.title: Fictional option E
sections.summary: One heading opens at a time.

blocks.text: Fifth invented section for the same reason. A reader can open one heading at a time. The other headings stay collapsed. This keeps a content-heavy fictional project from becoming one continuous scroll of every drawing and file.

Sixth invented section. It mentions a fictional bench, a fictional lamp, and a fictional aisle only as layout text. Those objects are not part of a built project. The tab control should still fit on one horizontal row that can scroll.

sections.title: Fictional option G
sections.summary: Collapsed cards keep the heading and one line visible.

blocks.text: Seventh invented section. Collapsing it leaves the heading visible and hides this paragraph. Keyboard arrows on the tab bar should move between Overview, Sections, Drawings, and Model and files without leaving the page.

Eighth invented section. Together with the others, the Sections tab stands in for a document that has many long parts. The drawings remain a separate tab, and the model link remains a separate tab. This fixture is not a client submission.
